??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Come in, come in, mind the pipe. It is hotter than it looks. Most things here are.
    - *Player*. Lux says the outer walls are glowing again. I went out to the Gate Walk last night to see. Amber, mostly. It was the right fog for it.
    - Starling sent down a note: the new lens is perfect, and the sky is enormous. Both of those were true before, but it is nice to hear.
    - *Player*. The little dark chip on my sill is still warm. Every morning I put my hand on it before the furnace is lit. Every morning, warm.
    - The furnace is drawing nicely. What did you want to look at?
        - *Choice:* How do you make the lantern colours?
        - *Choice:* What are those on the windowsill?
        - *Choice:* Is glass getting harder to make?
        - *Choice:* Nothing. I will let you work.
    - A pinch of this and that in the melt. Gold dust for rose, if you can believe it, though only a whisper. Copper for sea-green. The amber is iron and patience. Old Ignatius Fenn taught me at this furnace when I was small enough to sit on the sand bin.
    - Lux says amber carries furthest in fog. I say it depends on the fog. We have been saying it for years. Neither of us wants to win.
    - My failures. I am trying to make a glass that glows on its own, with no flame behind it. Powdered shells, rare sands, river stones, a powder from the apothecary, once some of Margo's spark-powder. That last one was loud.
    - None of them glow. They make very pretty paperweights, though. Hold one up to the window. There. You see why I keep trying.
    - Paperweights, all failures, all pretty. And at the end, the chip you brought up from under the city. It does not glow. It does not cool, either. I do not know what to make of that, so I have made nothing of it yet.
    - Good sand comes from outside the walls, on carts, and fewer carts come. So I melt down broken glass now. Old bottles, cracked panes, a whole crate that once got stuck halfway up Rivet's lift last winter.
    - It works. It is a little cloudy. I do not like it. But a cloudy lantern is better than a dark one, Lux says, and Lux is usually right about lanterns.
    - Go on. Look up at the lanterns on your way. Some of that light is mine.
